chains.title: Reduced GATA2 binding at an LMO1 regulatory element

links.claim: GATA2 is occupied at the variant and highly expressed in SK-N-SH; its QBiC-SELEX model predicts stronger binding to ref C than alt A. GATA3 also has occupancy and an independently supported ref-favoring prediction, so the evidence does not uniquely identify GATA2; this chain gives weight to its high expression and occupancy.
The variant lies in enhancer-like cCRE EH38E1518342, although its reported activity scores are maxima across biosamples rather than SK-N-SH-specific measurements.

LMO1 is a plausible target because the variant is intronic and the literature places the corresponding polymorphism in an LMO1 super-enhancer that modulates LMO1 expression in cis; regulation by this particular cCRE in SK-N-SH is not established.
GATA2 occupancy at the variant and high GATA2 expression are documented in SK-N-SH.
The LMO1 regulatory polymorphism is linked in the literature to neuroblastoma susceptibility, but GATA2-specific mediation is unproven; LMO1 is not a CRISPR dependency in SK-N-SH.

predictions: Allele-specific GATA2 occupancy at the variant should be greater for C than A in SK-N-SH.

If GATA2 mediates a regulatory effect, GATA2-specific perturbation should reduce the allele-dependent enhancer-output or LMO1-expression difference; the direction of that difference is not established.
falsified_if: A sensitive allele-specific assay finds no C-over-A GATA2 occupancy difference in SK-N-SH.
GATA2-specific perturbation leaves any allele-dependent regulatory difference intact, while GATA3-specific perturbation removes it.

chains.title: No TF-mediated effect of this variant on neuroblastoma
predictions: The in-vitro binding predictions and occupancy evidence will not translate into a reproducible TF-mediated effect of this base on enhancer output or LMO1 regulation in relevant neuroblastoma cells.

QBiC-SELEX screen of chr11:8233861:C>A, one line per TF, each with the TF's own or CIS-BP-mapped model of largest |z|. Candidates are TFs whose ENCODE ChIP-seq peaks contain the variant and that are expressed (DepMap line ACH-000149), bound here before bound elsewhere, then a strong site before a weak one, then by |z|; then expressed TFs ENCODE never assayed whose best model passes the gate (occupancy unknown). Shown: 10 of 12 occupied (5 with a strong site), 5 of 115 with unknown occupancy. Left out: 30 TFs assayed in the matching biosample and 529 assayed only elsewhere, none with a peak here; 2 bound but below 1 TPM. The gate (|z| > 4.05, Bonferroni over 997 models) marks a change QBiC-SELEX detects; it says nothing about occupancy. Effect > 0 means the alternate allele binds more strongly. In vitro binding only. Site strength is the better allele's best k-mer over the variant, as a percentile of the best model's k-mers; a strong site reaches the 97.5th. At a weak site the ChIP peak more likely reflects another site in the element.

We show that SNP rs[masked] G>T is the most highly associated variant (combined P = 7.47 × 10(-29), odds ratio 0.65, 95% confidence interval 0.60-0.70), and resides in a super-enhancer defined by extensive acetylation of histone H3 lysine 27 within the first intron of LMO1.

These findings indicate that a recently evolved polymorphism within a super-enhancer element in the first intron of LMO1 influences neuroblastoma susceptibility through differential GATA transcription factor binding and direct modulation of LMO1 expression in cis, and this leads to an oncogenic dependency in tumour cells.

A heritable polymorphism within regulatory sequences of the LMO1 gene is associated with its elevated expression and increased susceptibility to develop neuroblastoma, but the oncogenic pathways downstream of the LMO1 transcriptional co-regulatory protein are unknown.
